title: EDITORS Know Your Style! Editing LoRA Subspaces for Stylistic Attribution and Imitation
abstract: arXiv:2611.20846v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Disentangling writing style from semantic content is a fundamental challenge in literary text modeling. Style-content entanglement causes models to rely on semantic content for authorship attribution (AA) tasks and memorize author-specific content for style imitation (SI) tasks. We propose EDITORS (EditingLoRA Subspaces), a diagnose-then-deflate framework that adapts pretrained large language models and prioritizes stylistic features, making it effective for both AA and SI tasks. EDITORS first trains a diagnostic LoRA adapter using style-neutral statements derived from the training corpus to identify a content-oriented subspace. It then trains the final style adapter under activation-space deflation that projects input activations away from the identified content-oriented directions. We empirically demonstrate that EDITORS is effective. On three AA benchmarks spanning literature, social media, and news, EDITORS achieves state-of-the-ar

translated_title: EDITORS懂你的风格！编辑LoRA子空间用于风格归属与模仿
translated_abstract: 将写作风格与语义内容解耦是文学文本建模中的一项根本性挑战。风格与内容的纠缠导致模型在作者归属（AA）任务中依赖语义内容，并在风格模仿（SI）任务中记忆特定作者的内容。我们提出了EDITORS（EditingLoRA子空间），这是一个“先诊断后消减”的框架，它通过适配预训练大语言模型并优先考虑风格特征，使其在AA和SI任务中均能发挥作用。EDITORS首先使用从训练语料库中提取的风格中性语句训练一个诊断性LoRA适配器，以识别面向内容的子空间。然后，它在激活空间消减的条件下训练最终的风格适配器，将输入激活投影到远离已识别的内容导向方向上。我们通过实验证明了EDITORS的有效性。在涵盖文学、社交媒体和新闻的三个AA基准测试中，EDITORS取得了最先进的结果。
tldr: 提出EDITORS框架，通过“先诊断后消减”策略编辑LoRA子空间，将输入激活投影远离内容导向方向，从而解耦风格与内容，在作者归属和风格模仿两类任务上均取得最先进表现。
en_tdlr: EDITORS is a diagnose-then-deflate framework that edits LoRA subspaces by projecting input activations away from content-oriented directions, thereby disentangling style from content and achieving state-of-the-art performance on both authorship attribution and style imitation tasks.
